Subject: Draft MSA/Order Form - TFConvenience and Auto-Renew questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form last week. Legal at StormTech reviewed the redline and we have two items that are blocking procurement sign-off: the termination-for-convenience notice window and the auto-renew mechanics.

High level asks from our side:
- Can you confirm Redwood’s flexibility on the TFConvenience notice window — legal is pushing for 90 days; our procurement team wants 60 days.
- Auto-renew: we want a clear opt-out mechanism and a notice window (preferably 30 days) that will not automatically extend beyond one 12-month renewal without explicit agreement.
- If Redwood requires a longer notice window, can you offer a transition credit or prorated refund to mitigate operational risk?

Attached: redline_MSA_20251010.pdf and our comments in the order form.

I copied Natalie (procurement) to help with the rollout timeline. Can we get a short call tomorrow to resolve?

Best,
Elliot Harper
Director, Procurement
StormTech

Elliot / Natalie — thanks for the clear summary and for flagging procurement’s preference.

Quick response and proposal:
- Notice window: Redwood can accept a 60-day termination-for-convenience notice for the Order Form if the MSA TFConvenience section keeps 90 days for multi-year commitments; alternatively we can amend the Order Form to call out a 60-day notice for pilots and single‑year commitments and 90 days for multi‑year.
- Auto-renew: we agree to an explicit opt-out window of 30 days prior to the renewal term. We can add language that any renewal beyond one additional 12-month term requires written agreement.
- Commercial concession: for a 60‑day TFConvenience option we can offer a one-time transition credit equal to 5% of the remaining annualized committed spend (applies only to the first 45 days after effective termination) — this is a sign of good faith to address the operational lift you mentioned.

I’d like to loop in Ben for legal wording and Lauren for commercial signoff. Ben — can you review and confirm whether the split notice language (60/90 by commitment length) is workable and propose updated redline language for the MSA TFConvenience clause and the Order Form term block? Also flag any implications for SLA and refund mechanics.

Elliot — if that approach sounds OK I can send a redline by EOD and we can schedule a 30-min call to lock in wording.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Draft MSA/Order Form - TFConvenience and Auto-Renew questions

Folks — quick legal read. I made inline suggestions below and will push a redline draft after this note. High-level: the split 60/90 approach is acceptable but we should be explicit about which document governs (MSA baseline vs Order Form override). Recommend the following:

1) TFConvenience (proposed language) — single paragraph to add to MSA: "Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice; however, specific Order Forms may specify a shorter notice period (not less than sixty (60) days) for pilot or single‑term purchases, in which case the notice period set forth in the Order Form shall govern for that Order Form only."

2) Auto-Renew — add to Order Form: "The Term shall automatically renew for one (1) additional period equal to the expiring Term unless either party provides written notice of non‑renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then‑current Term. Any renewal beyond one (1) additional period requires mutual written agreement."

3) Refund / transition credit mechanics — if we offer the 5% transition credit, tie it to return of all customer data and completion of offboarding checklist within 45 days; credit applied to final invoice or as a one‑time credit on HubSpot invoice. This limits exposure and sets operational expectations.

4) SLA carveouts — termination for convenience should not void obligations to cooperate on data export; add a short continuity-of-service clause to the offboarding section.

I will attach the redline to the MSA and a one-page summary of the concession. Please review and tell me if any commercial pushback.

Ben Carter
Legal Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final proposal: notice windows, auto‑renew wording, and transition credit (summary)

Elliot / Natalie — thanks again for the patience. Following legal review here is the proposed text we can move to redline and DocuSign: please review and confirm by EOD Wednesday if this captures the commercial outcome.

Summary (what we will put in the MSA/Order Form):
- MSA TFConvenience baseline: 90 days' prior written notice.
- Order Form override: Order Forms for pilots or single‑term commitments may specify a 60‑day TFConvenience notice; the Order Form language will govern for that Order Form only.
- Auto‑renew: The Term will automatically renew for one (1) additional period equal to the expiring Term unless either party gives written notice of non‑renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then‑current Term. Any renewal beyond the single automatic renewal requires mutual written agreement.
- Transition credit: If StormTech elects a 60‑day TFConvenience option, Redwood will provide a one‑time transition credit equal to 5% of the remaining annualized committed spend, conditioned on completion of offboarding checklist and confirmation of data export within 45 days.
- Offboarding: Redwood will cooperate on data export and provide access to logs required for migration; termination will not excuse offboarding obligations.

Next steps:
1) If you confirm, Ben will push the redline and I will upload to DocuSign (link will be shared).
2) If you prefer a different credit mechanic (prorated refund vs credit), call out which option and we can adjust language.

Proposed short call: 30 minutes tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT to walk through any last items. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to closing ST deal.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
